Subject: Post-call recap & next steps - pricing + latency trade-offs

Hi Laura / Samir -

Thanks for the call today - good discussion. Below is a quick recap + the items we'll follow up on. Please reply with any corrections.

TL;DR: You're targeting a low-latency inference tier for fraud decisioning (p95 target in the 150-300ms range) with monthly token volume estimates between ~20M-50M tokens/month. Budget sensitivity: target unit economics around $50-$150 per 1M tokens depending on latency SLO.

Use case notes:
- Real-time risk scoring and decisioning in the request path (inline), plus some async enrichment tasks.
- Typical request: short prompt (~30-80 tokens) + model completion ~50-200 tokens (varies by flow).
- Peak QPS expected during market open - need predictable tail latency and no-thrashing during bursts.

Open pricing / qualification items we discussed:
- Confirmed estimated range: 20M-50M tokens/month (please confirm split between prompt vs completion tokens).
- Budget range guidance you gave: roughly $7k-$12k/month (you mentioned this as a starting point; want to confirm).
- Target unit economics: you called out wanting something like $/1M tokens target - let me know the target you need (e.g., $50, $100).
- Latency SLO: p95 target ~150-300ms - we'll evaluate Hosted low-latency tier vs Dedicated reserved capacity.

What we'll deliver next (action items):
1) I'll send a pricing worksheet with model tier comparisons (hosted low-latency vs dedicated), plus 1M/10M/50M token ballpark cost estimates. (attachment: redwood-pricing-worksheet.xlsx)
2) SLA and SLO options with trade-offs (attachment: SLA-options.pdf).
3) Ask from your side: sample prompts (5-10) + a representative traffic sample (per-minute distribution for a typical day) so Neha can size a perf pilot.
4) Schedule a 45-minute ops + SE session next week to run through performance expectations and pilot plan.

Key trade-offs to keep in mind (short):
- Streaming vs batching: streaming reduces tail latency for single-request flows but is less efficient cost-wise than batching for high-throughput workloads.
- Batching reduces $/token but increases per-request p95; good for async or tolerant flows.
- Dedicated capacity yields more predictable latency and unit costs at scale (best for >~30-40M tokens/month with tight p95).

Proposed next step: I'll send the worksheet by Monday and propose two slots for the pilot kickoff.

Thanks -
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Laura - great, thanks for confirming volumes and the target unit economics. Quick follow-up with ballpark pricing and guidance so we can align the pilot:

Ballpark pricing (illustrative) - standard hosted rates vs reserved dedicated:
- Hosted low-latency tier (no reserved capacity): ~ $125 per 1M tokens with p95 target ~150-250ms in our low-latency regions. This tier prioritizes routing to low-latency machines with higher unit cost.
- Hosted standard tier (cost-optimized): ~ $55-$80 per 1M tokens, p95 typically ~300-700ms depending on burst patterns (batching enabled).
- Dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit): starts to look attractive around 30-40M tokens/month - effective $/1M can drop to ~$45-$90 depending on committed capacity, model size, and quantization. Dedicated gives predictable tail latency (we can design for p95 <=200ms with the right config).

Latency vs cost notes:
- Streaming (token-wise or chunked streaming) reduces end-user perceived latency for single-turn flows but has lower batching efficiency - expect higher $/1M compared to fully batched throughput.
- Batching improves $/token significantly (often 30-60% savings) but increases p95; for inline fraud decisions, batching must be carefully tuned (micro-batches + short time windows).
- Autoscaling and burst handling: Hosted will gracefully degrade to slightly higher latency under extreme bursts; Dedicated with buffer capacity + burst policy is better for strict SLOs.

What I'm attaching: redwood-pricing-worksheet.xlsx (ballpark numbers for 1M/10M/50M tiers across hosted/dedicated + assumptions) and SLA-options.pdf (SLO tiers, uptime and credit terms).

Request for the pilot sizing (Neha): can you confirm -
1) typical prompt & completion lengths (avg + 90th percentile),
2) expected peak QPS and a 5-minute peak window QPS,
3) any hard data residency/KMS requirements.

Next steps: I'll book the pilot kickoff for Wed/Thu next week - proposing Wed 10:00am PT or Thu 11:00am PT. Which works better?

Best,
Marissa

Hi all - quick technical notes ahead of the pilot kickoff:

- For p95 <= 200ms with your token sizes (30-200 tokens total), we recommend either:
  * Dedicated with reserved GPUs + micro-batching (batch windows <= 10ms) and streaming enabled for critical paths, or
  * Hosted low-latency tier with pre-warmed pools and smaller model variants (quantized) for cost control.

- Typical config that balances cost/latency in similar customers: 2x gpus in a reserved pool for the steady state, burst to extra machines for peak windows (auto-burst policy), KV cache for repeated prefixes, and token streaming for final user-perceived latency.

- Pilot ask: please share 5 representative prompts and a 5-min peak QPS sample. If you can provide 1-2 synthetic payloads we can run an end-to-end perf test against a sandbox deployment.

I'll size a recommended Dedicated pilot (gpu count, estimated sustained throughput, and cost range) once we have the sample traffic. Happy to review the worksheet once Marissa shares.

Thanks -
